faqs.a: A lightweight markup language for formatted text: # makes a heading, **bold** bolds, - makes list items, and [text](url) makes links. README files, docs, and many blogs use it.
Yes - headings, bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code, fenced code blocks, links, images, unordered/ordered/task lists with nesting, blockquotes, horizontal rules, and GFM tables with alignment.
Yes. Raw HTML is escaped before rendering, links are restricted to safe schemes (http, https, mailto), and javascript: URLs are blocked, so pasted Markdown cannot run scripts.

keyFacts: Markdown Preview renders Markdown to styled HTML live as you type.
Supports headings, bold/italic/strikethrough, inline and fenced code blocks.
Supports links, images, nested bullet/numbered lists, and GFM task lists.
Supports blockquotes, horizontal rules, and GFM tables with column alignment.
Raw HTML is escaped and only safe link schemes are allowed - previews cannot run scripts.
Copy the rendered HTML or download the document as .html or .md.
markdown-preview.keywords: markdown preview, markdown editor online, markdown to html, live markdown preview, markdown cheat sheet
limitations: CommonMark plus GFM tables and task lists only: footnotes, definition lists, and math are not supported.
Raw HTML in the source is escaped, not rendered - by design, for safety.
Deeply mixed nesting (lists inside blockquotes inside lists) may render imperfectly.
The exported .html is a plain standalone page without site styling.

markdown-preview.workedExample:
Input:
# Shopping List
- [x] Apples
- [ ] Oranges
| Item | Qty |
| ---- | --: |
| Apples | 4 |

Live preview shows:
- A large "Shopping List" heading.
- A checked box for Apples, an empty box for Oranges.
- A table with Item left-aligned and Qty right-aligned.
- Word counter reads 8 words.
